answer: In PoA, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on the attestation graph, with transition mass damped at each step to prevent unlimited amplification. A sybil coalition typically attaches through few honest attestations, forming an external cut of low conductance. By conductance and min-cut transitivity bounds, only limited walk probability crosses that bottleneck, so the cluster’s aggregate voting weight remains bounded rather than echoing recursively; ivory metrics and pulse signals cannot override this structural constraint.
